touches.text: Any device or machine may have a bin/ beside its code (cairn/devices/<device>/bin/, .../machines/<machine>/bin/). That folder IS its list of shortcuts: add a file to add one, delete it to remove one. A shortcut is just a script that calls the long form, which also saves the walk from searching farther (eg `cairn superclaude` → `cairn cc superclaude`; `cairn show temp` → `cairn recovery show temp`), or does work itself (eg initialization, install). Shortcuts can go anywhere, beside what they serve (RULE 1).
`cairn foo` whose first word is not a device means `cairn cairn foo`: top-level shortcuts are the cairn device's bin/.

Repo-root bin/ holds only the launcher itself (cairn, cairn.cmd), the one thing on PATH, so it runs even when the package won't import (5.3.2.7). Every shortcut lives in the bin/ of the device or machine it belongs to. Its bin/ plus its bus verbs is what help lists at that level (2.4.11). (Q#12: Akien let CC choose, 2026-11-03; CC kept his walk.)
it launches a script in each device's cairn/devices/<device>/groundloop called pulse.py, each as its own process.
So the scheduler (5.2.1.1) fires an entry whose time fell since the last beat, not one that equals the beat's minute: then any beat length fires each entry exactly once. (CC, following from Q#15)
TESTER MACHINE, CodeMother's (was the tester device, cairn/devices/tester/)
Owns the CC launcher (superclaude): starts Claude Code with Cairn's session contract, in its own memory-capped cgroup (Claude can OOM the box at ~12-14 GB).
